discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics / topological quantum materials
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new, time-reversal-protected topological phase of matter, characterized by a Z2 invariant and helical edge states: the quantum spin Hall insulator. Molenkamp and co-workers realized this phase experimentally in 2007 in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, observing quantized edge conduction, and later demonstrated its nonlocal helical transport. Together these works established that ordinary band insulators can be topologically distinct. That insight launched three-dimensional topological insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, topological superconductivity proposals, and Weyl semimetals. This is a model of close partnership between theory and materials-based experiment. It opened a whole field rather than refining an existing one, and it produced robust, dissipationless edge channels with clear implications for low-power electronics and spintronics. The concept now underpins much of modern quantum-materials research worldwide.
